nodes.label: Manna (personal stewardship log)
nodes.rationale: Framed as a stewardship log rather than a budgeting app: the question it answers is 'have I given first,' not 'how much did I spend.' Single user by design.

nodes.label: manna-prototype.html as visual reference
nodes.rationale: Throwaway prototype kept as the canonical reference for layout, copy and flow only — explicitly not architecture, so its code is never a model to copy.

nodes.label: Offline-first PWA constraint
nodes.rationale: No native app. Logging must work with no network, because a log that fails when offline is a log that never happens.

nodes.label: The 5-second bar
nodes.rationale: Acceptance criterion for v1: log a real expense in under 5 seconds, offline, and see it correctly in Month after a reload. Chosen as a single falsifiable bar rather than a list of features.

nodes.label: PHP-only currency constraint
nodes.rationale: Currency is PHP only, 'no multi-currency, ever' — removes rate-at-time-of-transaction and cross-currency-total questions entirely.

nodes.label: Formal English copy constraint
nodes.rationale: All copy in formal English, no Tagalog: 'Motor upkeep' not 'motor gastos', 'Money borrowed and lent' not 'utang at pautang'.

nodes.label: Separate deployment, shared Tiswell database
nodes.rationale: Manna deploys separately from Tiswell but shares Tiswell's database, so one capture surface is not blocked on the other's release cycle.

nodes.label: Transaction (data model)
nodes.rationale: Amount, category (parent + optional subcategory), wallet, date, optional note, kind. debt_id and a no-category flag are added in v1 so the v1.5 Owed screen needs no migration.

nodes.label: Transaction kind (in / out / transfer)
nodes.rationale: Transfers never appear in category totals. Moving money to savings and paying down a debt both drop cash without consuming anything, so counting them as spending would make the reports lie.

nodes.label: Wallet (data model)
nodes.rationale: GCash, Cash, Maribank, GoTyme, Wise, Savings. Savings is a wallet and not a category; the Wallets grand total must answer 'what can I spend today', so anything not spendable stays out of it.

nodes.label: Category (parent + optional subcategory)
nodes.rationale: Expense parents: Food, Transportation, Housing & Utilities, Communication & Tech, Health, Personal, Giving, Learning, Leisure, Financial, Work. Income parents: Earned, Business, Passive, Other. Each parent owns a colour and an icon, both editable in Settings.

nodes.label: Debt (data model)
nodes.rationale: Person, direction (owe/owed), principal, opened date, optional due date, status. Payments are not new objects — they are transactions carrying a debt_id and no category — so balance is principal minus linked payments and partial payments need no extra code.

nodes.label: Recurring (template)
nodes.rationale: A template of category, amount, wallet and day of month that generates a monthly proposal; it does not create a transaction until approved.

nodes.label: Allotment (cap on a category)
nodes.rationale: A cap on a category — except Giving, which is a floor instead of a ceiling. That inversion is where the stewardship function lives.

nodes.label: Category Rule 1: two levels, never three
nodes.rationale: If a sub-sub is wanted, it is a note or a tag. Icon resolution is what makes this cost nothing visually: two levels still give every row a distinct shape.

nodes.label: Category Rule 2: parents stay at 8-12
nodes.rationale: Parents must fit one screen with no scrolling because a parent is picked on every log; a 13th is refused.

nodes.label: Category Rule 3: subcategory is optional
nodes.rationale: Logging to a bare parent must be one tap — a hurried log that gets sorted later beats a log that never happened.

nodes.label: Category Rule 4: merchants are never subcategories
nodes.rationale: 'Jollibee' goes in the note field; merchants as categories grow without limit and make reports meaningless. Currently unenforced — nothing counts three occurrences before allowing a new subcategory, and this is flagged as the rule most worth automating.

nodes.label: Icon resolution order (sub name, parent, fallback)
nodes.rationale: A subcategory has no colour or icon of its own; colour is inherited outright, while the icon resolves by the sub's own name first ('Dental' gets a tooth, not Health's heartbeat), then the parent's, then a fallback tag.

nodes.label: Central icon catalogue keyed by stable strings
nodes.rationale: Icons live in one catalogue in src/icons.tsx keyed by stable strings ('utensils', not a component). The key is what is stored on the category, so the underlying icon library can be swapped by editing that one file.

nodes.label: Home screen
nodes.rationale: Spendable total, reminders, month summary with pace against average, allotments running hot, today's transactions. Also carries the tithe strip.

nodes.label: Month screen
nodes.rationale: Six-month in/out chart, then categories ranked by amount with their subcategory breakdown.

nodes.label: Add sheet (built-in numpad)
nodes.rationale: Full-screen sheet from the centre button with a built-in numpad rather than the system keyboard, because the system keyboard covers the categories and forces you to type blind. Amount, note, wallet and categories are all visible at once.

nodes.label: Plan screen
nodes.rationale: Three tabs — Expected (approve or skip), Allotments (progress), Considering. Plan shows status, Settings holds the rules; Plan is deliberately not editable.

nodes.label: Wallets screen
nodes.rationale: Balances, spendable grand total, and a separate Owed panel kept out of that total.

nodes.label: Owed screen
nodes.rationale: Debts and loans in both directions with payment history. Scheduled for v1.5, but its schema hooks land in v1 to avoid a migration.

nodes.label: Settings screen
nodes.rationale: Categories, Recurring, Allotments, General. Settings holds the rules — it is the only place they can be edited.

nodes.label: Decision: no bank sync
nodes.rationale: Only a handful of PH banks are reachable by any aggregator, and those aggregators are B2B with contracts and compliance onboarding — not available to a solo developer.

nodes.label: SMS / notification capture as the automation path
nodes.rationale: If capture is ever automated it will be SMS or notification parsing on Android via MacroDroid or a small sideloaded listener posting to the API, which keeps Manna a pure PWA rather than forcing a native app.

nodes.label: Decision: recurring items are approved, not auto-logged
nodes.rationale: Silent monthly deductions are exactly the passivity the app exists to work against. The amount stays editable at the moment of approval, because bills vary.

nodes.label: Decision: no God/Others/Needs/Wants split
nodes.rationale: It existed, was then derived from the category, then removed entirely. Categories are the only classification and the split must not be reintroduced.

nodes.label: Decision: Giving is a normal parent category
nodes.rationale: Giving gets no special data-model status. The stewardship function is carried by exactly two things: the tithe strip on Home, and the Giving allotment being a floor while every other allotment is a ceiling.

nodes.label: Decision: to-buys here, to-sells in Tiswell
nodes.rationale: Manna owns money that moves; Tiswell owns things you have. A to-buy is money about to move, a to-sell is a possession — that is the boundary between the two apps.

nodes.label: Decision: Owed stays out of the spendable grand total
nodes.rationale: Money lent out cannot be spent. Rolling it in would turn the grand total into net worth, which answers a different question than 'what can I spend today'.

nodes.label: Out of scope list
nodes.rationale: No bank sync, no multi-currency, no receipt photos, no business ledger, no merchant-level categories, no third category level.

nodes.label: Build order (v1 / v1.1 / v1.5 / later)
nodes.rationale: v1 core ledger and screens; v1.1 recurring with approval, allotments, search, CSV export; v1.5 Owed. debt_id (nullable) and the no-category flag go into the v1 transaction schema specifically so v1.5 needs no migration.

nodes.label: Open question: moving a category between parents
nodes.rationale: Undecided whether moving a category between parents rewrites history or applies going forward only. Flagged to be picked deliberately rather than falling out of an implementation.
